envelope.author: nico
envelope.reason: A note only ever ended retracted, which says it was withdrawn with no successor; a note taken up into a concept or a unit has a successor, so retracting it misstates its history. It now ends resolved, naming what carries it. The sign is resolved, not superseded: supersession here already means a new version of the same entity.
envelope.cause: operator: retracting a weighed note is not conceptually coherent; it should point at the unit that carries it

payload.gloss: the set of notes: ideas, questions and decisions not yet canonical, the intake that the design and plans take up. Anyone may capture, revise, resolve or retract a note. A note taken up ends resolved, naming what now carries it, a concept or a unit; a note withdrawn with nothing carrying it ends retracted. A note's title is its name, one live note per title. Its kind is one of the note skill's labels (idea, question, decision), which the runtime never interprets. A live note that blocks a plan or unit is an **owed ruling**, the one sense of that sign; it blocks what it names until it no longer does, by being resolved, retracted or revised to block nothing, and a diverged note blocks whatever any of its versions blocks until it is reconciled.
